recognize_zh: 一顆比紅血球稍大的淋巴球，核佔滿細胞且表面有多條深溝與摺痕，呈腦回狀（cerebriform），染色質濃縮深染、細胞質極少，是 Sezary 細胞的典型外觀。
features: Lymphoid cell slightly larger than adjacent red cells
Very high N:C ratio with only a thin rim of scant cytoplasm
Nucleus with multiple deep grooves and folds producing a cerebriform (convoluted) contour
Dense, hyperchromatic condensed chromatin; no visible nucleoli
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a small to medium-sized atypical lymphocyte with a very high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio and scant cytoplasm. The nucleus is hyperchromatic with condensed chromatin and multiple deep linear grooves, producing a characteristic cerebriform appearance; nucleoli are not seen. Findings are consistent with a Sezary cell; in the appropriate clinical setting of erythroderma, confirmation of a clonal CD4-positive T-cell population with loss of CD7 and/or CD26 by flow cytometry is required for Sezary syndrome.

ddx.vs: Reactive lymphocytes have more abundant basophilic cytoplasm and only occasional shallow indentations, and flow cytometry shows no aberrant T-cell phenotype.
ATLL cells have polylobated flower-like nuclei with deep lobation rather than fine grooves, with HTLV-1 serology positive and frequent CD25 expression.
T-PLL cells have a visible nucleolus and cytoplasmic blebs with TCL1A rearrangement, whereas Sezary cells lack nucleoli.

ddx.dx: Mantle cell lymphoma or CLL with cleaved nuclei
ddx.vs: These are B cells expressing CD19/CD20 (with CD5 and cyclin D1 in MCL), whereas Sezary cells are CD4-positive T cells.
